texts: good. the cold wind, the striking, the struck Cliff Path and the night it happens at are all carried, and the multi-word name stays one symbol with "path" stated separately as its kind.

good. the Cliff Path is reused from the first sentence rather than introduced a second time, "on" is kept as the surface position rather than read as containment, and "salt-bloomed" is carried as one plain property of the lantern. Be aware that the coined word stays unanalysed — nothing connects it to "bloom" or to salt — so spell it the same way in every sentence and question that mentions it.

bad: the query hangs the lantern off a "to" oblique — the slot for what an action is aimed at — so it never asks what befalls the lantern and can match nothing in the knowledge base; an open "what happens to X?" has no supported form at all, because the slot an answer would file X in depends on the verb the question leaves unnamed. Name the event you are asking about and give the lantern its plain object position, with no "to"-phrase: "Does the cold wind damage the salt-bloomed lantern at night?" If you would rather keep the question open, ask it from the acting side, which is supported: "What does the cold wind do at night?"
